back: GDP measured at constant (base-year) prices, so it changes only when the volume of output changes.

front: Give three uses of national income statistics.
back: Measuring growth and spotting recessions; planning government spending and taxes; comparing living standards over time and between countries; guiding firms' investment.

front: Give five limitations of national income statistics.
back: Double counting; the informal sector; unrecorded non-market activity; inaccurate data; price changes (and they ignore distribution and quality of life).

front: Why does the informal sector make GDP understate output?
back: Informal businesses keep few records and are not registered, so much of their output is never recorded.

front: Can GDP rise while GDP per head falls?
back: Yes: if the population grows faster than GDP.

front: Why is GDP per head an imperfect measure of living standards?
back: It is an average: it hides inequality and ignores leisure, health, education, pollution and resource depletion.
